channel.title: UX on Eriol Does Design
channel.description: Recent content in UX on Eriol Does Design

item.title: An accessible User Interface to build custom smart home IoT
item.description: Ensuring that electronics and coding proficient interfaces intended for beginner users are accessible, usable and approachable to new users with ESPHome.

item.title: Music listening behaviour in Smart Homes. Improving the smart speaker music management experience
item.description: Improving controls for a music player that is connect to local smart home devices and speakers where we prioritise management of audio across a home’s smart ecosystem.

item.title: Measuring the usability of complex OSS installation methods for new users
item.description: How to better understand ‘approachability’ on complex, technical installation methods on new users and users with less technical familiarity and proficiency research

item.title: Helping Journalists open suspicious documents safely
item.description: Helping journalists and activists stay safe from potentially infected files with a simple, straight-forward and understandable OCR based tool that ‘scans’ your suspicious document and makes a ‘clean’ copy.

item.title: How developers understand package security information: UI for Attestations
item.description: Working with the Linux Foundation’s OpenSSF/Securing software repos working group on understanding attestations and developing an open source attestation style guide.

item.title: Understanding the lives of Designers contributing to OSS with diary studies
item.description: The research project ‘The Secret Lives of Designers contributing to OSS’. A 12 week diary studies user research and resulting industry report.

item.title: Sending files without a trace. Using the magic wormhole protocol for peer-to-peer file transfer
item.description: Helping NGO’s, Journalists and Activists stay safe when sending essential files over the internet by making sure they understand and can operate peer to peer file sharing tools.

item.title: Coming together as an OSS community to keep foundations and essential OSS funded.
item.description: Supporting the foss responders project by ensuring we had great visual design and indentity that prompted donations and design assets and styles that supporting fundraising and communication efforts.

item.title: Making sense of global data about Malware and Spyware searchable, viewable and understandable
item.description: Making sense of global data about Malware and Spyware searchable, viewable and understandable to journalists, activists and academics.

item.title: Designing safe, private and care-focused mutual aid experiences in times of crisis
item.description: Just before the COVID-19 pandemic hit, a team of technologists explored and prototyped what a safe, secure, connected and crisis-relevant mutual aid technology network would need to look like.

item.title: Providing essential coaching during prototype funding rounds for open source software
item.description: Making the most of limited coaching time with open source software projects that are in prototyping funding rounds is an exercise in getting to the root of a design and usability problem and quickly and efectively as possible.

item.title: Strengthening the Design community and the Open Source Ecosystem by faciltating collaboration together and bridging the design gaps in OSS
item.description: A community interest, multi-stakeholder project focussed on bringing designers into the OSS ecosystem and solving the puzzle of sustainable and maintainable open source design contributions via ‘OSS for good’.

item.title: The Usability and Design challenges of scientific and research open source software
item.description: A 6 month funded project to interview people making and maintaining scienctific and research OSS and how they understand Usability and Design challenges.

item.title: Communication during crisis. Building technology the connects you in the most extreme crisis
item.description: After team members were trapped during a terrorist attack, we never wanted to not be able to check on our team during high risk crisis again. Making crisis communications usable and well designed for stress scenarios.

item.title: Comprehensible data matching across humanitarian data sets using HXL and the Humanitarian Data Exchange
item.description: Ensuring that import, export and tagging of data on the Ushahidi data collection platform was usable and accessible to users as they imported and exported datasets across systems. Universal data language comprehension as critical usability for data analysis.

item.title: How can technology and design help people striving for peace after genocide
item.description: How can technology help people striving for peace after genocide and how to focus on a co-creation, liberty and equity focus strengthen bridges between communities under traumtic stress.

item.title: Maintaining the open source design community and sustaining the growing need for better design across open source software globally
item.description: Maintaining the open source design community and sustaining the growing need for better design across open source software globally.

item.title: Resources for developers to improve usability testing skills under pressure
item.description: Making usability testing make sense for small, resource-constrained technology teams and the developers that prop up the open source internet freedom ecosystem..

item.title: Website information routes that prioritise what users are seeking
item.description: Reworking The Open Technology Fund’s website that prioritised understanding who visits and for what purposes.

item.title: Technology for farmers and sustainable food supply chains with The Open Food Network
item.description: Giving farmers and sustainable food supply chains open and accessible technology to sell food to their communities.

item.title: Data Collection, Mapping and Crisis Response technology for open source and social good globally
item.description: Building Data Collection, Mapping and Crisis Response technology for global NGO and Activists in the heart of Kenya.

item.title: Making sense of student accomodation for students starting their educational journey
item.description: Ensuring cohesive design across a braod spectrum of platforms, projects, promotions and communications as the in-house design team at unite students.

item.title: Sensible restrictions for screentime for kids and supporting design that empowers the parent and kid relationship and doesn't re-enforce control
item.description: Leading the visual and UX design projects for a popular parental control app worldwide across iOS, Android and webapp.

item.title: Giving Science Annuals a visual creative make-over with interactive, reactive covers and rich visuals
item.description: Creating unique and reactive print design annuals with rich visual explorations for content internally and maximising the wonders of print design.

item.title: Prototypes to improve the user experience and service design of end of life care for a person with a terminal illness
item.description: Inclusive, trauma informed prototypes that explore the stresses, joys, struggles and day to day of people with terminal illness and their carers.

item.title: Working alongside the community with mapping the green map spaces locally
item.description: Working over 4 years of research, community co-creation to develop a community led greenmap project that could be accessed online and in person as a permenant sign.
